title: Canonical closed-point counit and normalized module projection arrows
statement: Use the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] and the geometric morphism and mate convention of [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. For a scheme X, write Gamma_X for evaluation at the final etale object, epsilon_X for the geometric morphism to sets with constant-sheaf inverse image [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and, for a geometric point x [def-weil-geometric-point], use its stalk/skyscraper geometric morphism [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. For a scheme map a:A→S use the existing sheafified Kan-extension inverse image [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Define imageGerm_{a,x}:Gamma_S→(ax)^{-1} by the inverse-image adjunction unit, the canonical direct-image identification of global sections, and the germ at x. Given d:Gamma_S≅(ax)^{-1}, define the inverse-image counit (ax epsilon_B)^{-1}→b^{-1} by d^{-1}, the canonical constant-sheaf pullback isomorphism, and the constant-sheaf counit; closedOrientation is its direct-image mate. For any geometric morphism f of site topoi and commutative ring Lambda, a module lift consists of an adjunction on sheaves of modules over the sheafification of the constant Lambda-ring [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], natural identifications of its underlying set functors with f^{-1} and f_*, agreement of the adjunction hom-equivalences under those identifications, and the following normalization of module operations: for every generalized element, the adjoints of z=r x+y satisfy the same identity for every constant scalar r, acting through the ring-sheafification unit. For module lifts p_L,s_L and e:s_{L,*}p_{L,*}≅Id, define unitComparison:p_{L,*}→s_L^* by applying p_{L,*} to the s_L-adjunction unit and then applying e. These are definitions of the specified arrows and interfaces, with no invertibility or exactness asserted.
